 NBA Roundup: Doncic, Jokic deliver Cup wins, Sengun posts triple-double

 Luka Doncic and Franz Wagner headline a busy Friday night across the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season and Emirates NBA Cup 2026
 By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net 
 Nine games counted toward both the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season and the Emirates NBA Cup on Friday, including the Los Angeles Lakers rallying from an 11-point deficit in the second half and narrowly holding to beat the Sacramento Kings 106–104 at crypto.com Arena. Slovenia’s Luka Doncic drove the push with 25 points, eight assists, four rebounds, and two steals. Georgian reserve Sandro Mamukelashvili threw in nine points and nine rebounds off the bench. For the visitors, Lithuanian starter Domantas Sabonis produced a 19-point, 16-rebound double-double, Israeli Emanuel Sharp got three points, and Ukrainian-Belarusian Alex Karaban stayed on the bench.
 At Ball Arena, Serbian superstar Nikola Jokic took over in the fourth quarter to end up with 26 points, 11 assists, and seven rebounds as the Denver Nuggets overpowered the Houston Rockets 133-124. Back on the floor from a recent left eye corneal injury , Turkish starter Alperen Sengun paced Houston with a 28-point, 11-rebound, 10-assist triple-double. In contrast, Serbia’s Bogdan Bogdanovic did not score in a brief showing off the bench.
 The closest finish took place at Barclays Center. “Not the best look, but we’ll take it,”  underlined German Franz Wagner in his postgame press conference, after sinking a jumper with 2.4 seconds left in the fourth quarter to give the Orlando Magic a 113–111 win over the Brooklyn Nets . The 25-year-old forward led all scorers with 35 points. “Got some good open looks early on and was able to knock them down,” Montenegrin reserve Nikola Vucevic described hitting all five of his shots for a season-high 15 points. “This is a huge adjustment. Just a few months ago I was playing 30 minutes a game, starting, being one of the main options on a team, and now coming into a very, very, very different role.” German Tristan da Silva added six points, and Georgian Goga Bitadze had four.
 For Spaniard Jordi Fernandez’s side, Israeli Danny Wolf got 20 points. Fellow starter Nolan Traore of France tallied four points before leaving early with a right hamstring injury. Off the bench, Russian Egor Demin recorded six points, while German Moritz Wagner ended up with three in his first NBA game against his brother, Franz, but Israeli Ben Saraf did not play. “We were struggling with rebounding and with our defense, and I felt like Danny was playing well,” explained 43-year-old Fernandez about moving Wolf into the lineup in place of Demin. “I liked the effort and purpose that everybody had in the game.” 
 “It was very weird seeing him over there,” confessed the Magic leader on taking on Moe. “Playing five years together, you get super used to that. It kind of set in. Kind of realized today that he’s on a different team. It was weird, but it was also fun. I think he’s in a good spot. I think he really likes it here, so, um, happy for him.” 
 Hezonja, Diabate, Zubac, Mara double-double
 The Cleveland Cavaliers erased a 14-point deficit and built a 24-point cushion in the fourth quarter on their way to a 128–119 win over the Indiana Pacers at Rocket Arena. James Harden erupted for 51 points, with Croatian backup Mario Hezonja grabbing ten rebounds to go with ten points, edging out the opposing starting center and fellow Croatian international Ivica Zubac, who finished with 21 points and ten boards.
 The Atlanta Hawks pulled off a similar turnaround at State Farm Arena to beat the Charlotte Hornets 111–97. “Just trying to figure out how to sustain our lead. I don’t think any other team that we played are better than us,” reacted French starter Moussa Diabate after posting a 21-point, 15-rebound double-double. “Right now we’re not liking what we’re doing, we’re not getting what we want, but when it turns around it’s going to be a whole different energy.” In bench minutes for Charlotte, Germany’s Christian Anderson Jr. and France’s Tidjane Salaun registered four points each, but German Hannes Steinbach did not check in.
 The Oklahoma City Thunder climbed out of a 16-point hole at Paycom Center to top the New Orleans Pelicans 126–120 behind 40 points from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.  “I’m just trying to play every day as tough as I can,” stressed Spanish starter Aday Mara after his 22 points and 16 rebounds. Fellow European starters Ajay Mitchell of Belgium and Isaiah Hartenstein of Germany chipped eight and five points, respectively, but Serbian Nikola Topic missed the game with a left hip strain. On the wrong end, Croatian reserve Karlo Matkovic went scoreless.
 At United Center, the Washington Wizards overcame a 15-point deficit to edge the Bulls 98–94 behind 36 points from Anthony Davis. French starter Alex Sarr managed three points, and French reserve Bilal Coulibaly added two. Lithuanian starter Matas Buzelis netted nine points for the Bulls , while French reserve Noa Essengue made all three of his shots for eight points despite minor wrist soreness.
 Serbian Darko Rajakovic guided the Toronto Raptors past the Detroit Pistons 105–102 to snap a six-game skid. Austrian starter Jakob Poeltl put ten points, including a late tip-in before Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley closed out the win at Little Caesars Arena.
 Finally, the Phoenix Suns took down the Utah Jazz 111–101 at Delta Center. Ukrainian reserve Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk netted 11 points but was limited to the wrong end. As announced before tipoff, Bosnian teammate Jusuf Nurkic will remain sidelined with a toe injury for at least another week.
